'84; dispatched to France and Germany '84 to study naval arsenal affairs; on commission to bring home the Matsushima, built in France '90; Naval Constructor-Commander '97; Rear-Adm. '02; Vice-Adm. '03; Commander of Kure Admiralty '05-09; Pres. of the Japan Steel Works '10-14 Add. Omori, near Tokyo.

Marquis, Capt. of Infantry (ret.); was b. in '76 of the former fief of Tosa; graduated from the Military Cadet School in '00; to France for study '09 to return home ill in '10; married in '03 Princess Sachiko, eldest daughter of Prince Fushimi (d. '19). Add. Yoyogi, near Tokyo.

Viscount (cr. '87), was b. '37 in Yamaguchi, and was one of those young men who with late Prince Ito and Marquis Inouye proceeded to England on the eve of the Restoration for study; returned home in '70 and appointed Secretary at the Public Works Department and finally rose to be its Minister in '80; subsequently appointed Vice-President of the former Senate; Councillor at the Court; President of the Legislative Bureau; Lord Steward to the House of Princes Arisugawa and Kitashirakawa, etc. Resigned the official service in '93 and has since been leading retired life. Add Toriizaka, Azabu, Tokyo.

Vice-Pres. of the Tokyo Chamber of Commerce, Dir. of the Nippon Marine Eng. Co., b. '64. Hiroshima-ken; came up to Tokyo '84, and opened a small diving firm; est. Yamashina Marine Eng. Office which was subsequently amalgamated with the Mitsubishi Marine Eng. Dept., is engaged in harbour works, bridge and dock construction, reflotation of wrecked ship, etc.; visited U.S.A., as representative of the Chambers of Commerce in Japan '18. Add. 1-chome, Kobikicho, Kyobashi, Tokyo.

Admiral, ex-Com.-in-Chief of First Fleet; was b. in '63 in Yamagata-ken; graduated from the Naval Academy '83; and Sub-Lieutenant '85; Commander '98; Captain '06; Rear-Admiral '08; Vice-Admiral '12. Was Member of the Naval General Staff; on the Staff of the Imperial Headquarters; Chief of Staff to the 1st Squadron and then to the Saseho Naval Station; chief of the 2nd Section of the Naval Materials Dep't, etc; President of the Naval Academy '10-14. Deputy Chief of the Naval Staff Board and Mem. of the Adm. Council in '14-15; Com.-in-Chief of Saseho Admiralty in '15-17; Admiral '18. And. Yokosuka.

of Yamashita Steamship Co. which has sprung into fame since the outbreak of the War, was b. 1866 in Iyo, and came up to Tokyo while under 20 to seek employment. In '98 he became a small coal-dealer; began shipping business in '03, next lumber and warehouse business. The war and unusual activity of shipping business has established his fortune. Add. Takanawa, Shiba, Tokyo.

D.C.L. Mem. House of Peers and ex-Pres. of Adm. Litigation Court; b. in Fukui '49; studied in Germany '70-72. He afterward filled various high civil posts and occupied the Presidency, Adm. Liti. Court '06-13. Mrs. Fusako Yamawaki is a lady educationist and Dir. of Girls' High School. Add. Hinoki-cho, Akasaka, Tokyo.

Governor of Yamanashi-ken 1916-'18; b. '71 in Kyoto adopted son and heir of the above; grad. Law, Imp. Univ. in '96 and passed the higher civil service examination the same year; official in the Dep't of Agr. and Com., first as Per. Sec. to the Minister, then as Secretary and Sectional Chief; Commissioner of Anglo-Japanese Exhibition in '10; the Dir. of Monopoly Bureau, Formosa, chief Commissioner to Panama Exhibition in '14-15. Add. Hirakawacho, Koj., Tokyo.

Vice-Admiral, Mem. of Admirals' Council since '18. b. in '66 in Tokyo; graduated from the Naval Academy '86 and then the Naval College '87; Navigating-Lieutenant of the transport Saikyo Maru during the Japan-China War; Captain '05; Chief of Staff to the 4th Squadron during the Russo-Japanese War; Rear-Admiral '09; Chief of the Bureau of Personnel '09-13; Pres. of Naval College '13-14; Com. of 1st Fleet Aug., '14 and partook in the war, then transferred to Com. of 3rd Flotilla Feb. '15; Vice-Chief of Naval Staff Board '15. Add. Hommura, Azabu, Toky.

Treasurer, Imp. Household; b. in '68 at Saga; grad. from Imp. Tokyo Univ. (Law) '96, and at the same time passed the higher civil service exam.; Tax Inspector '97 attached to Nagasaki Taxation Office; transferred to Finance Office to be made its Sec. '00; Dir. of Finance Bur., then Debt Bureau. Add. Yoyohata, near Tokyo.

Count, Mem. House of Peers, Mem. of Japanese Census Commission, Consulting Statist to the Cabinet, mem. of International Statistical Society, Hon. Mem. of Royal Statistic Society (England), etc.; b. '70 in Echigo, son of Lord Mitsu-aki, scion of the House of Yanagisawa which hereditarily held the fief of Koriyama, Yamato; adopted '86 as son and heir of the Main houses, and succeeded to the title '93; grad. at the Peers' College with honour '94; sent by the Imperial Court to Germany for study and attended the Universities of Berlin, Vienna, Strassburg, Brussels and Paris, studying statistics; meanwhile appointed on the suite of H.H. Prince Kan-in who was sent to attend the Diamond Jubilee of Emperor Francis Joseph; returned home in '00; attended the International Statistical Conference six times as representative of Japan, from that at Christiania in '99 to the latest at the Hague '11. He held Presidency of the 1st Mutual Insurance Co. till '15, and is now its adviser. Add. 8-chome, Tamachi, Shiba, Tokyo.

Paymaster-Lieut. (ret.), Vice-Gov. of Hypothec Bank of Japan; b. in '67 in Nagasaki-ken; graduated from the College of Law, Imp. Tokyo Univ., '90. Entered the Bank of Japan immediately after graduation; travelled Europe in '96; was appointed Chief of the Issue Dep't, Auditor to the New York Agency, Chief of the National Loan Bureau; resigned '13, and appointed Dir. of the Hypothec Bank; present post '13. Add. Harajuku, Tokyo.

Dir. of Kinjo Middle School, author, and retired diplomat; b. '50 in Oita prefecture; graduated from the Keiogijuku, '70; entered the central Government as Secretary to the Treasury, '78; resigned with Count Okuma in '81 and took charge of the Hochi Shimbun, in company with the late Mokichi Fujita; took part in the formation of the Kaishinto (progressive party); made tour in Europe and America, '86-88; Master of Ceremonies and Chief of the Bureau of Imperial Tombs, '90-96; Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary to China, '97-98; placed on the retired list in '99. He has written "Keikoku Bidan" (story of ancient Greece), "Ukishiro Monogatari" (a marine novel); "News Society," etc. Add. Harajuku, Tokyo.

Pres. and Mng.-Dir. of the 1st Mutual Life Insur. Co., was b. '65 in Okayama; grad. the Third Higher School in '89; entered the Japan Life Insur. Co., and in '93 was made manager of the Kyosai Life Insur. Co.; went over to Belgium to attend the International Congress of Actuaries held in Sept. '95; and afterward entered a German Life Insur. Co. to receive its business training; was appointed an official in the Dep't of Agr. and Com., but soon resigned to start the present Co. Add. Omori, near Tokyo.

Baron (cr. '16), Adm., Mem. Sup. Mil. Council.; b. '60 in Aichi; Naval Ensign in '85, and rapidly promoted; was elevated to Captain in '01 and finally to the present rank. Long served as Staff-Officer of the Standing Squadron, then Attaché to the Legation at Petrograd, and Vice-Com. of the Yashima, commanding the Asama in Russo-Japanese War; Dir. of Naval Staff College '12-13; Com. of Maizuru Admiralty '13-'14; Minister of Navy '14-15; Admiral '16; Com. 2nd Fleet '17. Add. No. 81 Kogaicho, Azabu, Tokyo.

Manager of the Shibusawa's Office, Dir. of the Shinagawa Fire Brick Co., Shibusawa Warehouse Co., etc., was b. '73 in Uwajima, Iyo; grad. Tokyo Higher Commercial School in '94; appointed Per. Sec. to Baron Shibusawa. He travelled once in Europe and America with the Baron. Add. Shirokane-Daimachi, Shiba, Tokyo.

a millionaire banker who sprang from obscurity to the present affluence, b. '38 in Toyama-ken: started as an apprentice at a shop in Tokyo and finally opened an exchange shop on his own account, finally developing it into a bank; has founded several other banks and has moreover lent his powerful backing in the starting of the Tokyo Fire Insurance Co., the Imp. Marine Insurance Co. and Kyosai Life Insurance Co. He has financed several useful undertakings and was a Mem. of House of Peers. Add. Yokoami-cho, Honjo, Tokyo.

a highest tax mem. House of Peers for Tokyo, General Supervisor of the Yasuda Bank etc. run by the Yasuda family; b. in '69 at Uwajima, eldest son of Chusuke Iwomi, and was adopted by the Yasuda family as husband of its oldest daughter; grad. from Law, Imp. Univ., Tokyo, '94. Add. Yoko-ami, Honjo, Tokyo.

Member of Privy Council since 1916, was b. '59 in Fukuoka-ken. Grad. from Keiogijiku, the Chu Shoin at Hongkong and finally from Cambridge Univ. in England; Prof. in the 3rd Higher Sch in '89; Secretary to the Cabinet; Councillor to the Legislation Bureau; Director of General Education Bureau in '97; Chief Secretary to the Cabinet '98; Member of House of Peers from '0[illegible] to '16; Vice-Min. of the Dep't of Agr. and Com. in '01; resigned in '11. Add. Sadowamcho, Ushigome, Tokyo.

a highest tax-payer, mine-owner, Dir. of several Cos.; b. '49 in Chikuzen; studied at the Keiogijuku '72; has made a fortune in coal-mining; founded single-handed the Meiji Semmon College in 1903 by contributing 3,000,000 yen, and has been rewarded for it with 3rd class of the Sacred Treasure. Add. Wakamatsu, Fukuoka.

Dir. of Mitsui Bussan Kaisha. b. '70 at Kashiwahara, Kyoto; grad. from the Osaka Higher Commercial School in '89 and entered Mitsui Firm the same year; was promoted to Dir. '17, after having been Chief of one Branch or other. Add. Tsukudo-Hachiman, Ushigome, Tokyo.

Pres. of Tokyo Wire Mfg. Co., Mng.-Dir of the Tokai Leaden Pipe Mfg. Co., b. '68, Ehime-ken; came up to Tokyo '88, and attended to study as self-supporting student; taught at a commercial school, Yokohama till '96, when he entered business as an Accountant of the Yokohama Wire Mfg.; its Manager '10; left the Co. when it was absorbed by Furukawa Co.; promoted the present cos. '12. He has connections with several other cos. Add. No. 17 Okanocho, Yokohama.

Dr. Agr., Prof. at Agr. Coll., Imp. Tokyo Univ. and Pres. of Tokyo Agr. Univ. (private); b. '60 in Kumamoto; grad. from above Coll. '83; studied in Germany '99-02; expert to the Agr. and Com. Dep't; Prof. in '94. Add. Aoyama Minamicho, Tokyo.

D.C.L. (Japan), Judge of Supreme Court since '01; b. '62 in Nagano-ken; grad. from Law, Imp. Tokyo Univ., class '88; sat at Tokyo, Chiba and Hakodate District Courts, and Tokyo and Hakodate Appeal Courts before his transfer to the present post; teaches at the Waseda Univ., etc. being an authority on claims; was sent abroad on official mission '09. Add. Nakano, near Tokyo.

Baron. (cr. '15). Pres. of the Supreme Court since '06; was b. '50 in Oita-ken; entered the judicial service '76, Public Procurator '80, the acting Dir. of Criminal Bureau and Sec. of the Dep't which post he resigned to study law in Europe '86-91; was appointed on return Pub. Proc. of the Tokyo Appeal Court, Councillor, then Vice-Min. of Justice '96, Proc.-Gen. '98, Chief Pub. Proc. of Tokyo Appeal Court '99. Add. Kagurazaka, Ushigome, Tokyo.

geologist, D. Sc. (Japan), Prof. in the Imp. Tokyo Univ.; was b. '60 in Nagasaki; grad. Geology in the Imp. Tokyo Univ. and was subsequently appointed an official at the Dep't of Agr. and Com. in '82; sent to Germany to prosecute further study in '86; appointed Prof. at his alma mater on returning home. Add. Higashi-Goken-cho, Ushigome, Tokyo.

veterinarian, principal and proprietor of the Azabu Veterinary School; was b. '61 in Kagoshima; studied veterinary science at the Agr. Coll., Imp. Tokyo Univ., and further in America; appointed Prof. in the Agr. Col. of the Imp. Tokyo Univ, '87, which he resigned some years ago to start his own veterinary school in Tokyo. Add. Shirokane, Sanko-cho, Tokyo.

Prop. of the Yonei Firm, Dir. of the Meiji Gum Co., the Kirin Beer Brewing Co., etc.; was b. '61 in Okayama-ken; grad. from Keiogijuku; then entered business and established exp. & imp. business at Ginza, under style "Yonei Shoten." Add. Kaminibancho, Koj., Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. of Kobe Marine, Transport and Fire Ins. Co., and of Nissin Fire and Marine Ins. Co., b. '66 in Ishikawa-ken; became a lawyer '87; elected Vice-Chairman of Osaka Lawyer's Association '99; gave up the profession and became Mng.-Dir. of Kobe Marine Ins. Co. '07; organized Nisshin Co. '11. Add. Kyomachi Hondori, Nishi, Osaka.

Mng.-Dir. of Mitsui Bank, was b. '68 at Numazu; studied in America '90-95, and entered the Nippon R'ly Co., removed to the Mitsui Bank which sent him abroad '00 to inspect banking business '02; Chief of the Yokohama Branch 1903 and next that at Osaka '08; Mng.-Dir. '10. Add. Aoyama Minami-cho, Tokyo.
Chief of Police Bureau, Household Dep't, was b. '45 in Ishikawa; held local posts at Kagoshima etc.; Dir. Finance Bureau, Imp. Household. Add. Shimonibancho, Koj., Tokyo.
Pres. of 7th High School, b. '70 in Ishikawa; grad. from Philosophy, Imp. Tokyo Univ. '97; was Dir. of Middle Schools, Prof. at Waseda, etc. Add. Kagoshima.

ex-Minister to Siam; b. '59 in Kumamoto-ken, attaché in '86, appointed to The Hague Legation in '88, Per. Sec. to Minister of Education in '93 and then Prof. in Third High School, 2nd Legation Sec. at Vienna in '98, removed to The Hague in '00, and transferred to Vienna in '01 till '04; Minister to Siam in '05, relieved in '14. Add. Foreign Office, Tokyo.

member of the Board of Ceremonies, Imp. Court, b. '50; clerk at Foreign Office in '77-86, attaché in '87, Élève-Consul at Manila in '92 and then attaché in Berlin; Personal Sec. of Foreign Office '96-'18. Add. Tokyo.

Secretary of Chinese Legation since '16, was b. '74 in Niigata-ken; grad. from Coll. Literature (English Lit.), Imp. Tokyo Univ. '99; passed the Dip. and Com. Service Exam. the same year; attached at Seoul '99; Elève-Consul at Amoy, Shanghai, London, etc, '00-06; 1st Secy. at London '10; Consul-Gen. at Hankow. Add. Hiroo, Azabu, Tokyo.
Commander (ret.), 2nd Count, mem. House of Peers, Pres. Japan Lifeboat Assoc., was b. '55; studied in England, and then grad. from the Naval Cadet School in '80. Add. Sagacho, Fukagawa, Tokyo.

Dir. of the Bank of Japan, was b. '63 in Kagoshima. Early entered the Bank of Japan in which he gradually distinguished himself to be given in course of time an important position of Director. Add. Kita-iga-cho, Yotsuya, Tokyo.

Count (cr. Vis. '96 and Count '07), ex-Vice-President of Privy Council '12-16, b. '41 at Tokushima; entered the civil service early in the Meiji era and after having held various posts in the Treasury, Home Office and elsewhere was appointed the Gov. of Tokyo-fu and then Vice-Min. of Home Affairs. Then began his Ministerial career, first as Minister of Edu., '90; Justice, '91-93; Home Affairs '93-96; Communication twice '98-00 and '01-3; Home Affairs '04, which last he had to resign in connection with the Sept. 5th, '05 anti-Peace Agitation in Tokyo. Add, Miyamura-cho, Azabu, Tokyo.

Adm., Mem. of Supreme War Council; b '59 in Kochi-ken; appointed Sub.-Lieut. in '83; was at one time Staff Officer of the Kure Adm., Sec. Chief, Staff Office; Chief Staff of Saseho Adm.; Com. of the Naniwa, Takasago, and some others; Rear-Adm. in '07; Vice-Adm. '09; Prof. of Naval Staff Coll. in '10; Com. of 2nd Squad. in '11-12; Chief of Edu. Board '12-14; Com. of the Kure Adm. '14-17; Com.-in-Chief of 1st Fleet '15-17; full Adm. '16; present post in 17. Add. Navy Office, Tokyo.

Pres. of the Yoshimura Firm, b. in '58 in Shiga-ken; came up to Tokyo to seek employment when 29 and worked his way up to the present eminence; inaugurated the present firm in '91. He is connected with the Manchuria Flour Mill and Nippon Machine Mfg. Co. as their President, etc. Add. 2-chome, Shirokane-Dai-Machi, Shiba, Tokyo.
Pres. of 5th High School; b. '76 in Yamaguchi; grad. from Law, Imp. Tokyo Univ. '99; was Prof. at 2nd High School, Inspector, etc. Add. Kumamoto.

millionaire dealer in iron and copper and importer and exporter in Kyoto, b. in Kanazawa '77, brother of Mr. S. Hayakawa, banker, and was adopted by the Yuasa of Kyoto; grad. from Law, Imp. Tokyo Univ. '91. Add. Takakura Higashi-iru, Gojodori, Kyoto.

mem. House of Peers (nom. '16), b. '74 in Fukushima, grad. from Law, Imp. Tokyo Univ. '89; held posts of Secretary at Shiga, Hyogo and other provinces; then Secretary and Dir. of Local Government Bureau, Home Office; Gov. of Okayama and then of Shizuoka in '14; Dir. of Police Bur., Home Office '15-16 Add. Shizuoka.

general exporter and importer in Kobe, And. of Masuda Flour Mill Co. and Mem. of Kobe Chamber of Commerce ; b. '69 in Wakayama-ken ; was a Mng. of the well-known Masuda Firm., Yokohama, Add. Yamamoto-dori Gochome, Kobe.

ex-Vice-Min. of Com. 1914-16, Dir. of the Yusen Kaisha ; was b. in Shizuoka ; grad. Law Coll, Imp. Univ. '93, and was long connected with the Com. Dep't having been Secretary, Dir. of Maritime Bureau. etc., Dir. of the Fujita Firm, Osaka. Add. Fujita Firm, Osaka.

Pres. of Higher Female Normal School, Tokyo ; b. '63 in Saga ; first studied Medicine at Imp. Tokyo Univ., but left it unfinished in '84 ; held post of prof. at various Gov. Schools, Dir. of Middle Schools, Dir. Imp. Music Academy '08-17 ; present post in '17. Add. Ichigaya, Ushigome Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen. ex-Com. of 15th Division ; b. '63 in Kochi ; Sub-Lt., '82 ; graduated from Military Staff College ; studied in England, Vice-Chief Staff of 2nd Army in Russo-Japanese War ; Com. of 27th Brigade '09 ; Sec. Chief of General Staff till '14, when transferred to Dir. of Mil. Staff College ; above post in Jan. '15. Chief of Staff of the Siberian Expedition sent during the Great War.

Prop. and Edit. of the Herald of Asia, started by him in '16, an English weekly review of life and progress in the Orient ; b. '62 in Hoki Province, and grad. Sapporo Agr. Coll. '84 ; was long on the staff of the Japan Mail : entered civil service for a short while and was twice appointed Per. Sec. of the late Prince Ito when he was Premier; frequently visited Europe and America ; was during the Russo-Japanese War a resident correspondent of the London Standard in Tokyo ; accompanied the late Prince Ito to Seoul as non-official mem. of the Residency-Gen., and in January '06 he took over the Seoul Press formerly owned by an Englishman. Withdrew from it in '09, to start the Oriental Information Agency in New York City, but returned to Tokyo in December '10 to assume the control of the Japan Times, from which he withdrew in '14. Made a tour to U.S.A. with Baron Shibusawa in '15. Add. Hommuracho, Azabu, Tokyo.

Director of the Taiwan Sugar Co., was b. '54 at Kagoshima ; studied at an American Coll. '73-79 ; Sec. of the former Public Works Dep't '79 ; transferred to the R'ly Bureau '83 and remained in the service as Dep't Dir. till '09 when he was placed on retired list. Add. Ochiai-mura, near Tokyo.

Founded 1881; publishes monthly organ Dai Nippon Nokai-ho, and maintains Tokyo Agricultural University (private) in Tokyo as its educational institution. Members number 15,500 and are Honorary, Special Ordinary and Associate. Patron Prince Fushimi; Pres. Marquis K. Matsudaira; Vice-Pres. Dr. A. Yokoi, the Pres. of the University. Add. Tameike, Akasaka, Tokyo.

Pioneer association of the kind in Japan and was est. about 1880 by the late Sir Earnest Satow and others in Japan for studying and investigating Japanese customs, history, literature, etc. List of members 530 including those residing abroad. Annual subscription ¥12; Meeting held quarterly and proceedings published occasionally and distributed to members gratis. Pres. Sir William Conyingham Greene; Hon. Secy. Ernest Wilson Clement. Add. Keio University, Tokyo.

Founded 1900; funds ¥150,000 to be created. Subscription in proportion to the capital paid up of the associated banks, ranging from ¥100 to ¥1,000. The members number 69 banks. Pres S. Hayakawa, Directors. T. Matsukawa; Chief Secy. N. Yamazaki. Add. Sakamoto-cho, Nihombashi, Tokyo.

Founded June, 1896; issues a monthly periodical; members numbered 1,700 at the end of Feb. 1916; Dues, ordinary membership 20 Sen per month. Directors Y. Ishiyama, S. Ikeda, K. Harada, T. Hanai, etc. Add. Nishi-Hibiya, Kojimachi, Tokyo.
Founded 1882; publishes a monthly Botanical Magazin. Dues ¥6.60 per annum. Members number 400. Pres. Dr. J. Matsumura; Chief Dir. Dr. K. Shibata. Add. Botanical Garden, Tokyo.

n: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, Division of Economics and History, Japanese Committee
t: Est. in July, 1912 in accordance with the international Conference of Economists held in 1911 in Berne. The result of investigation will be published at the head office in New York, U.S.A. President of the National Committee is Baron Y. Sakatani, and Secy. Y. Yamamoto. Office at Senshu Daigaku, Kanda, Tokyo.

Founded 1878; dues for regular member ₹5 per annum, associate ₹3, these numbering 650 in all. Publishes a monthly Tokyo Kwagakukwaishi. Pres. U. Suzuki; Secy. Y. Shibata, K. Aso. Add. Science College, Imp. University, Tokyo.
Founded 1912; subscription ₹4 to 500 a year. Pres. R. Kimura; Vice-Pres. Dr. I. Nakahara; Chief Secy., B. Kawanishi. Add. Sanchome, Yurakucho, Kojimachi, Tokyo.
Founded 1914; subscription ₹10 per annum. Members number 5,000. Pres. Marquis S. Okuma; Vice-Pres. J. Soyeda; Chief Secy. S. Hayakawa. Add. Sanchome, Yurakucho, Kojimachi, Tokyo.
Created 1907; annual subscription according to the business result of the society. Chairman of the committee is K. Kagami; Chief Secy. K. Takai. Add. Minami-Nabecho Nichome, Kyobashi, Tokyo.
Founded 1886; member 466 in all. Representatives, K. Ikeda, K. Otani, O. Suzuki; Secy. T. Ikeda. Add. 7 Sojurocho, Kyobashi, Tokyo.

Founded 1879; number of members 260; dues ₹100 in lump or ₹6 a year. Patron Prince Kan-in; Pres. Marquis N. Nabeshima; Vice-Pres. Visc. Y. Hanabusa, Baron D. Kikuchi; Secys. Dr. F. Omori, K. Inouye, K. Fukuchi. Add. Nishi Konyacho, Kyobashi, Tokyo.
Founded 1899. Dues ₹2 a year. Members number about 800; publishes a monthly organ Rekishi-Chiri. Pres. Marquis M. Hachisuka. Add Aoyagicho, Koishikawa, Tokyo.

Founded 1889; publishes a monthly magazine. Dues for ordinary members ₹2, special members ₹3, per annum; list of members some 3,000. Pres. Marquis S. Okuma; Vice-pres. Viscount T. Fujinami. Add. 696 Nakashibuya, Tokyo.

Founded 1914; members 7,000 in March, 1916. Dues, regular member ₹100 in lump or annually ₹12 for ten years, common member ₹10 or 3 annually for five years. Pres. Marquis S. Okuma; Vice-Pres. Baron Y. Sakatani. Add. Yurakucho 1-chome, Tokyo.

Founded 1898; publishes as organ Teikoku Tetsudo Kyokai Kwaiho; members 2,436 in all. Honorary members confined to those who have rendered distinguished services to railway business. Pres. Count M. Terauchi; Vice-Pres. Dr. H. Furukawa, Dr. K. Nomura; etc. Chief Secy. R. Unno. Add. Marunouchi, Tokyo.
Founded 1896; publishes a monthly journal; subscription, ₹12 per annum. Pres. Viscount Kaneko; Vice-Pres. S. Asano. Add. 1 Yamashirocho, Kyobashi, Tokyo.
Founded 1894; annual dues ₹2; members some 300 at present. Pres. Dr. Baron Chincho Hozumi; Dirs. T. Minobe, G. Suehiro. Add, c/o Hozumi, Hanikata-machi, Ushigome, Tokyo.
Founded 1908; publishes a quarterly bulletin; subscription to be levied in proportion to business result of the Cos. Pres. Taizo Abe. Add. Yurakucho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo
Founded 1882; publishes monthly magazine. Dues, ordinary member ¥2 per annum; members number 337. Pres. Dr. S. Nakamura. Secys. W. Oishi, T. Okada, T. Yoshida. Add. Meteorological Observatory, Tokyo.

Founded 1885; publishes a magazine as its organ. Dues, ordinary member ¥6 annually and ¥3 for admission; supporting member is asked to contribute ¥200 or upward in lump; members 1,500 in all, including 18 honorary members and 66 supporting members. Pres. Dr. W. Watanabe. Add. Kagacho, Kyobashi, Tokyo.

Founded 1898, for developing resources in Formosa, Korea and Manchuria. Has established schools in Tokyo, Seoul, Dairen, etc. bringing up students to devote themselves to colonization work. Subscription ¥6 per annum for ordinary member; issue monthly magazine, Toyo Jiho; members number 3,500. Pres. Komatsubara, ex-Minister of Education; Vice-Pres. Baron Okura; Dirs. M. Kadono, S. Hayakawa. Add. Marunouchi, Tokyo.

Founded 1892; publishes a Japanese monthly and a French Bulletin as its organ. Reliable information is supplied on application to foreigners abroad. Special member ¥10 in lump or ¥12 in course of 4 years, and ordinary ¥1.50; members number 165,477. Patron Prince Kanin; Pres. Viscount K. Kiyoura. Add. Nishikicho, Kanda, Tokyo.

n: Society for the Propagation of Roman Alphabets
t: Founded —; publishes its organ in Roman letters; Members 3,000; Dues, ¥1 per annum. Pres. Marquis K. Saionji. Add. No. 3 1-chome, Yurakucho, Kojimachi, Tokyo.

n: Society for Protection of Industrial Property
t: Founded 1905; dues, ¥5—30 in lump or ¥2 a year. Pres. Viscount K. Kiyoura; Vice-Pres. K. Otani. Add. Yurakucho, Kojimachi, Tokyo.

Founded 1878; publishes monthly magazine styled Tokei Shushi, and also issues the Imperial Japanese Statistic Annual and a number of statisctics. Dues, ¥3 a year and have membership of 500. Pres. Dr. Baron Yoshiro Sakatani. Add. Yamashita-cho, Kyobashi, Tokyo.

Founded 1886; admits graduates of Imperial Universities of Tokyo, Kyoto, Kyushu and Tohoku, and also others who have connections with the above institutions. Dues, ¥2 per annum, or ¥20 for life; publishes monthly bulletin; comprises 18 committees and 1 chief secretary. Add. Nishikicho, Kanda, Tokyo.

Founded 1879; annual subscription ¥6 for class "A" member. ¥3.60 for "B" member; members number about 400; the Zoological Magazine is issued monthly, with "Annotations Zoological Japonensis" as occasional publication. Pres. Prof. S. Watase (c/o Imp. Univ. Tokyo); Secy. Dr. N. Yatsu.

Est. 1906 by Japanese who have stayed in America and by Americans staying in Japan, with the object of promoting friendly relation between the two countries. Number of members about 300; annual dues ¥12. Pres. Viscount Kentaro Kaneko. Add. Gofukucho, Nihombashi, Tokyo.
Founded 1889; members number about 74 comprising only those who have studied in Belgium. Secy., Mr. S. Akusada, 53 Fujimicho, Azabu, Tokyo.

Found 1908 by the late Count Hayashi, the late Sir Claude MacDonald, Count Hirosawa, the late Capt. Brinkley, Viscount Inaba, Vice-Admiral Baron Miyabara, Count Kawamura, etc.; dues ¥5 a year for ordinary members or ¥50 in one sum for life. The membership numbers about 250. Add. British Embassy, Tokyo.

Formed in 1914 by graduates and friends of Waseda University as social organ. Membership about 300; dues ¥24 a year; one half for country member; Pres. Dr. Y. Hiranuma. Sec. S. Tamura. Add. Eiraku-cho, Tokyo. Tel. Central 389.

Founded 1885. List of members number over 300 including five grades of members; dues of ordinary member ¥3.60 a year. Patrons, Prince Nashimoto and French Ambassador; Chief Dir. K. Furuichi, Dr. Eng. Add. Hibiya Park. Tokyo.

Founded 1902; covers British India, French Indo-China, Dutch islands in the South Seas. Members 570 in all. Pres. Marquis S. Okuma; Vice-Pres. Baron N. Kanda, Dr. F. Nanjo; Secy. Y. Soyejima. Add. Hibiya Bldg., Hibiya Park, Tokyo.

Founded 1879 by graduates of and others instructed in Keio University and is a social club. Entrance fee ¥300; annual subscription ¥36. Membership over 1,000. Pres. E. Kamada; Chief Dirs. J. Kadono, H. Ishikawa. Add. Nabecho Nichome, Kyobashi, Tokyo.
Created by Japanese interested in Central and South Americas, or peoples of these republics connected with this country, about 120 in number. Add. Hibiya Park, Tokyo.

Est. 1888 by Japanese; is a non-political institution. List of members about 500 including country members. Entrance fee ¥30, annual subscription ¥36. The present building was built in 1906. Pres. Viscount C. Okabe; Hon. Secy, Mr. S. Hayakawa. Add. Yurakucho, Kojimachi, Tokyo; Tel. No. 625 & 5439 Honkyoku.

Founded 1906; members number 350; dues, ¥6 a year for ordinary members or ¥200 for life, special members ¥500. Pres. Count M. Terauchi; Vice-Pres. Baron S. Goto; Add. Uchisaiwaicho, Marunouchi, Tokyo.

Est. 1885 by Japanese and foreigners; entrance fee ¥50; annual subscription ¥36 for city members and ¥10 for country members. List of members about 300. The present building was built in 1908 at the cost of ¥300,000. Pres. H.H. Prince Kan-in; Vice-Pres., British Ambassador, Baron Makino, Mr. Sonoda; Hon. Secy. Mr. A. Medley; Hon. Treas. Mr. M. Kushida. Add. Aoicho, Akasaka, Tokyo. Tel. No. 225—7 & 760 Shimbashi.
Tamayacho, Nishi-ku, Nagoya. Est. 1896; cap ¥2,210 p.u; in '18 absorbed Kitakata and other banks, cap. being greatly increased. Pres. Y. Watanabe.

n: Asano Chuya (Day and Night) Bank, K. K
t: Tori-1-chome, Nihombashi, Tokyo. Cap. ¥5,000 (3,000 p.u.). Pres. M. Shiraishi, Mng.-Dir. Y. Watanuki.
